newsitem.title: UK: BA expected to be confirmed for Heathrow T5.
newsitem.headline: BA expected to be confirmed for Heathrow T5.

text.p: British Airways Plc is expected to be confirmed on Thursday as tenant for airport operator BAA Plc's giant fifth terminal at London Heathrow, according to industry sources.

They said details were likely to be announced by BAA on Thursday, even though the future of the project is still in the balance, with what is proving to be Britain's longest ever public planning inquiry.
The inquiry has already been running since May 1995 and is not now expected to be completed before 1998.

BAA has said the 1.5 billion stg project is vital if Britain is to maintain Heathrow's position as Europe's most important international airport, increasing capacity at the airport by 30 million passengers a year. Last year, Heathrow handled nearly 56 million passengers but BAA and its airlines say the airport is now close to full and without T5 would lose incremental traffic to continental European hubs such as Amsterdam, Paris and Frankfurt.

But local authorities, residents and environmental groups opposing the plan say a fifth terminal would lead to an intolerable increase in aircraft noise, road traffic and pollution. -- Greg Mahlich, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
